reference.source: Sports medicine and emergency medicine references
clinicalPearls: A dilutional fall in serum sodium developing during or up to a day after prolonged endurance exercise
The main mechanism is excessive intake of hypotonic fluid, often compounded by inappropriate secretion of antidiuretic hormone
Mild cases may be asymptomatic, while severe cases cause nausea, headache, confusion, seizures and life-threatening cerebral oedema
It can be mistaken for dehydration, and giving more hypotonic fluid worsens it
Severe symptomatic cases are treated with hypertonic saline, not with additional free water
Prevention centres on drinking to thirst rather than overdrinking during endurance events
reference.pathophysiology: Exercise-associated hyponatraemia develops when total body water is in excess relative to sodium, chiefly from drinking hypotonic fluid beyond what is lost. Non-osmotic release of antidiuretic hormone during prolonged exercise impairs the ability to excrete the excess water, and failure to mobilise sodium stores contributes. The resulting fall in plasma osmolality drives water into cells, and cerebral oedema produces the dangerous neurological manifestations. Because the problem is water excess rather than sodium deficit, hypotonic fluids aggravate it.
additionalDifferentials: Other causes of hyponatraemia (SIADH, adrenal insufficiency)
additionalInvestigations: Point-of-care or laboratory serum sodium measurement
Assessment of fluid intake during the event and body-weight change if known
Exclusion of other causes of collapse such as heat stroke and hypoglycaemia
redFlags: Altered mental state, seizures or signs of cerebral oedema
Rapidly falling or very low serum sodium
reference.prognosis: Mild cases resolve with fluid restriction, and severe symptomatic cases usually respond to prompt hypertonic saline; delayed recognition with cerebral or pulmonary oedema can be fatal.
pitfalls: Assuming dehydration and giving hypotonic fluids that worsen hyponatraemia
Failing to use hypertonic saline for severe symptomatic cases
Encouraging overdrinking as a prevention strategy
management: Treat severe symptomatic disease (confusion, seizures, cerebral oedema) with hypertonic saline to reverse the fall in plasma osmolality
Manage mild or asymptomatic cases with fluid restriction and observation, allowing spontaneous water excretion
Avoid giving further hypotonic or free water, which worsens the dilutional state
Monitor serum sodium closely during correction and perform serial neurological assessment
Provide airway protection and seizure control in severe cerebral oedema
Exclude other causes of exercise-associated collapse such as heat stroke and hypoglycaemia
Prevent recurrence by advising athletes to drink to thirst rather than overdrink during endurance events
